title: Two of the same type without replacement
source: S1 Ch4 theory S1-4.5 Quick check 2 (4 red, 6 blue, both red)
stem: Two counters are selected at random, without replacement, from a bag containing {r|int} red counters and {b|int} blue counters. Find the probability that both counters are red.

Two tickets are drawn at random, without replacement, from a box containing {r|int} winning tickets and {b|int} blank tickets. Find the probability that both tickets are winning tickets.

title: Total probability from a two-branch tree
source: S1 Ch4 theory S1-4.5 Quick check 3 (card 0.40 receipt 0.08, cash receipt 0.03)
stem: A shopper pays by card on {p|int}% of visits and by cash on the other visits. The shopper is offered a receipt on {u|int}% of card payments and on {v|int}% of cash payments. Find the probability that the shopper is offered a receipt on a randomly chosen visit.

contexts.stem: A commuter travels by bus on {p|int}% of mornings and walks on the other mornings. The commuter is late on {u|int}% of bus mornings and on {v|int}% of walking mornings. Find the probability that the commuter is late on a randomly chosen morning.

A caller uses a mobile phone on {p|int}% of calls and a landline on the other calls. The call is answered on {u|int}% of mobile calls and on {v|int}% of landline calls. Find the probability that a randomly chosen call is answered.

steps.name: tot
steps.text_tex: \(\mathrm{P}(\text{late})\) is the sum of those two probabilities.

contexts.stem: A messenger cycles on {w|int}% of deliveries and walks on the other deliveries. The messenger is delayed on {a|int}% of cycling deliveries and on {b|int}% of walking deliveries. Given that a delivery is delayed, find the probability that the messenger cycled.

A host offers the theatre on {w|int}% of invitations and the cinema on the other invitations. An invitation is accepted on {a|int}% of theatre offers and on {b|int}% of cinema offers. Given that an invitation is accepted, find the probability that the theatre was offered.

title: A survey of photos and viewing

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF (the official tree diagram is reconstructed in TeX without vertical rules, with the same labels; complement branches are left unlabelled as in the QP). Steps and marks from the official MS PDF. Both parts are numeric (x=0.15 and 0.427). Fully numeric, not mixed. The official stem contains the phrase one-week holiday; that wording is kept because the no-week rule applies only to the site teaching schedule and UI, not to official paper stems.

stem:
\(\begin{array}{cccc} & \text{Take fewer than 100 photos} & & \text{View fewer than 3 times}\\
x & & & \\
 & & 0.76 & \text{View at least 3 times}\\
 & \text{Take at least 100 photos} & 0.90 & \text{View fewer than 3 times}\\
 & & & \text{View at least 3 times}\end{array}\)

A survey is undertaken to investigate how many photos people take on a one-week holiday and also how many times they view past photos. For a randomly chosen person, the probability of taking fewer than 100 photos is \(x\). The probability that these people view past photos at least 3 times is 0.76. For those who take at least 100 photos, the probability that they view past photos fewer than 3 times is 0.90. This information is shown in the tree diagram. The probability that a randomly chosen person views past photos fewer than 3 times is 0.801.

steps.name: p0_eqn
steps.text_tex: Form an equation from the two routes to viewing fewer than 3 times, equal to 0.801.
steps.note: MS: M1 equation with a sum of two two-factor probabilities equal to 0.801.

parts.stem: Given that a person views past photos at least 3 times, find the probability that this person takes at least 100 photos.

steps.name: p1_num
steps.text_tex: \(\mathrm{P}(\text{at least 100 photos and at least 3 views})=0.85\times 0.1=0.085\).
steps.note: MS: B1 0.85 times 0.1 seen on its own as numerator or denominator of a fraction.

steps.name: p1_den
steps.note: MS: M1 attempt at P(at least 3 views), either (0.85 times p1 + 0.15 times p2) or 1-0.801, seen anywhere.

steps.name: p1_form
steps.text_tex: \(\mathrm{P}(\text{at least 100 photos given at least 3 views})=\dfrac{0.85\times 0.1}{0.85\times 0.1+0.15\times 0.76}=\dfrac{0.085}{0.199}\) (or denominator \(1-0.801\)).
steps.note: MS: A1 correct unsimplified P(at least 3 views) as numerator or denominator of a fraction.
